holdings.retrieved_scope: Five NVIDIA snapshots 2022-Q4, 2023-Q1/Q4, 2024-Q1/Q2; not every quarter or current portfolio.
holdings.value_quality_warning: Reported raw 2023/24 values appear thousand-scaled although the SEC renderer labels nearest dollar. Do not produce dollar allocations or portfolio weights from these rows until units and possible amendments are reconciled.
holdings.exposure_warning: Call underlying share counts are separate; no strike/expiry/delta or short book. Split adjustment mandatory for June 2024.

crosschecks.claim: Nvidia AI enthusiasm in June 2023 is consistent with independently reported ownership.
crosschecks.support: SEC common share counts support continuing exposure around the public thesis; Q1 count exceeds Q4 2022.
crosschecks.limits: Snapshots do not establish exact June exposure, entry date, price or claimed doubling.

crosschecks.claim: Nvidia common shares increased from March to June 2024 because the raw count increased.
crosschecks.support: 10-for-1 split means June 214,060 equals 21,406 pre-split shares, far below March 175,943.
crosschecks.limits: Change in snapshot quantity does not give every execution or any derivative offsets.

crosschecks.claim: The later phrase sold it proves a complete Nvidia exit by June 2024.
crosschecks.support: June filing still reports 214,060 common shares. The phrase supports a major sale but not a verified zero position at that snapshot.
crosschecks.limits: A complete sale and re-entry between dates is possible but unproved; no exact sale date asserted.

crosschecks.claim: Long-horizon June 2023 Nvidia conviction guaranteed no subsequent trimming.
crosschecks.support: He later calls the sale a departure from his stated plan; SEC confirms a major reduction.
crosschecks.limits: Conflict at plan/behavior level, not proof the AI thesis was false. Options and full net risk remain unknown.

crosschecks.claim: Equity 13F exposure proves Druck's portfolio was net bullish on all risk assets.
crosschecks.support: Rates, currency, short exposures and funding are largely absent.

case_chains.decision_attribution: Druckenmiller's 2015 account identifies his idea/initial short and Soros's sizing intervention. Credit is shared; do not count this as an independent additional macro case.
case_chains.predecision_evidence: No authenticated contemporaneous manager memorandum retrieved.

case_chains.case: 1999 internet short and 2000 emotional tech re-entry
case_chains.outcome_class: major adverse with two distinct episodes, selected retrospectively
case_chains.selection_reason: Famous failure revealing timing/path risk and emotional override, not a fabricated universal rule.
case_chains.decision_window: 1999 early-year short; January to spring 2000 exit/re-entry
case_chains.predecision_evidence: No authenticated pretrade memo found. Contemporary May 2000 reporting retrospectively describes earlier private meetings through unnamed participants; it is not an original decision log.

episode_1.position_and_outcome: Lost Tree account: approximately $200m internet short in 1999 produced approximately $600m loss. These are rounded self-reports, not audited net-year returns.

episode_2.position_and_outcome: Same account: January 2000 tech exit followed by approximately $6bn spring re-entry and approximately $3bn loss over six weeks. Do not describe either amount as personal wealth loss.

case_chains.retrospective_motive: First-person 2015 and original 2026 interview attribute re-entry to emotion after watching others profit, despite an earlier exit.
case_chains.contemporaneous_crosscheck: May 2000 reproduced WSJ report independently describes tech losses and the 2000 departure, with provenance/fidelity limitations.
competing_explanations: Timing and margin risk in the earlier short
Different PM books and the aggregate fund
Emotional re-entry is a later admission, not an independently dated motive
case_chains.audit_lesson: Distinguish a too-early short from a later long-at-top error. A correct sale and known discipline do not protect against an unlogged emotional reversal.
missing: Full security ledger and offsetting hedges
Audited episode attribution and manager authority limits

case_chains.outcome_class: supplementary major positive with premature-sale regret, selected retrospectively
case_chains.selection_reason: Independent SEC positions plus a public thesis during ownership; useful to constrain narrative versus actual holding behavior.
case_chains.predecision_evidence: No authenticated pre-entry memorandum. The 2026 account describes learning from partner/AI specialists, buying shortly before ChatGPT, then scaling up; this timing and motive remain retrospective.
case_chains.actual_position_evidence: Five SEC snapshots establish reported common-share holdings; Q4 2023 also reports calls separately. No inference about the whole risk book.
case_chains.during_trade_public_view: June 7, 2023: contemporary reporting records a bullish AI/Nvidia thesis and possible multi-year holding horizon.
case_chains.outcome_evidence: Original 2026 interview self-reports a roughly sixfold equity gain and regret at selling too soon. SEC snapshots independently confirm ownership and later sharp reduction, not realized returns.
case_chains.behavior_limit: June 2024 filing retains a common-share residual; no complete-exit claim. Snapshot counts must be split adjusted, and option risk cannot be inferred from underlying counts.
competing_explanations: Market beta and AI sector rerating
Analyst-team input rather than personal engineering expertise
Position changes, options and execution prices are unobserved
A successful retrospective anecdote has winner-selection bias
case_chains.audit_lesson: Connect the changing business thesis to dated issuer evidence, then separately test risk and exit behavior. A multi-year statement is a revisable plan, not a guarantee.
missing: Independent realized P&L and full-risk attribution

confidence.reported_holdings: high for reported quantities, subject to filing accuracy

abstention_rules: Do not copy extreme leverage or concentration anecdotes into an ordinary user portfolio.
Do not infer historical fund performance from a 13F replication backtest.
Do not use stale chart-pattern success rates as current validated rules.
Do not force an equity answer when the view concerns currency/rates/liquidity.

temporal_packet_policy.historical_vs_benchmark: Case ex-ante date and benchmark method date are different tests. A 2018 book can inform a 2026 method but cannot become a 2007 contemporaneous source merely by describing 2007.
temporal_packet_policy.current_undated_pages: Exclude their current-version content from historical decision packet unless a dated pre-cutoff replacement establishes the claim.
temporal_packet_policy.filings: A quarter-end observation is usable only after its public filing timestamp, subject to amendments/confidential disclosure. Q4 2025 holdings filed in 2026 must not appear in beginning-2026 selection.
